title_en: The battery boom is quietly rewiring the grid
excerpt_en: For most of the past century, electricity behaved like a delivery business. Batteries have begun to change that arithmetic — and with it, the economics of who gets paid for keeping the lights on.
body_en: For most of the past century, electricity behaved like a delivery business: generate it somewhere, push it down a wire, and hope it arrives before anyone asks where it came from. Batteries have begun to change that arithmetic. In the past five years the cost of a grid-scale lithium-iron-phosphate pack has fallen by roughly half, and installations have multiplied faster than most forecasters expected.

The consequence is subtler than a cheaper phone. A battery is not a generator; it is a temporal arbitrage machine. It buys power when the grid is drowning in midday solar and sells it back when the evening peak arrives, capturing a spread that used to belong entirely to gas plants.

That spread is now the subject of an unglamorous but fierce contest. In California, where storage capacity has grown from almost nothing in 2018 to more than ten gigawatts, the evening price spike has flattened noticeably. Traders who once made a comfortable living from the six o'clock scramble have found their margins compressed.

Yet the boom has an awkward dependency. A battery earns money only if the gap between cheap and expensive hours is wide enough. As more capacity is installed, that gap narrows — the very success of storage undermines the returns that justified it. Engineers call this cannibalisation; investors call it the reason they have suddenly become cautious.

The second constraint is less visible. Grid operators have discovered that a fleet of batteries behaves nothing like a power station. It responds in milliseconds, which is wonderful for frequency regulation, but it also means that software, not concrete, now determines whether the lights stay on. Regulators trained to inspect turbines are being asked to audit code.

None of this makes the transition less inevitable. It makes it messier. The cheapest electricity system humanity has ever built is also the most computationally complex, and the institutions that govern it were designed for a world in which power flowed in one direction only.

enrich.title_zh: 电池热潮正在悄悄改写电网
enrich.summary_zh: 电网级储能成本五年腰斩，加州傍晚的电价尖峰被明显削平。但储能越成功，套利空间越窄，这正是它最大的软肋。文章指出真正的变化不在设备，而在于电网的调度权从混凝土转向了代码，而监管体系仍停留在单向送电的旧世界。

paragraphs.en: For most of the past century, electricity behaved like a delivery business: generate it somewhere, push it down a wire, and hope it arrives before anyone asks where it came from. Batteries have begun to change that arithmetic. In the past five years the cost of a grid-scale lithium-iron-phosphate pack has fallen by roughly half, and installations have multiplied faster than most forecasters expected.
paragraphs.zh: 在过去一个世纪的大部分时间里，电力更像一门配送生意：在某个地方发电，沿电线输送出去，然后指望它在你追问来源之前抵达。电池已经开始改变这道算术。过去五年，电网级磷酸铁锂电池组的成本下降了约一半，装机量的增速超过大多数预测者的预期。

paragraphs.en: The consequence is subtler than a cheaper phone. A battery is not a generator; it is a temporal arbitrage machine. It buys power when the grid is drowning in midday solar and sells it back when the evening peak arrives, capturing a spread that used to belong entirely to gas plants.
paragraphs.zh: 其后果比一部更便宜的手机要微妙得多。电池不是发电机，而是一台时间套利机器。它在正午光伏泛滥、电网不堪重负时买电，在晚高峰来临时再卖回去，赚取一段过去完全属于燃气电厂的价差。

paragraphs.en: That spread is now the subject of an unglamorous but fierce contest. In California, where storage capacity has grown from almost nothing in 2018 to more than ten gigawatts, the evening price spike has flattened noticeably. Traders who once made a comfortable living from the six o'clock scramble have found their margins compressed.
paragraphs.zh: 这段价差如今成了一场不起眼却激烈的争夺。在加利福尼亚，储能装机从 2018 年的几乎为零增长到逾 10 吉瓦，傍晚的价格尖峰被明显削平。那些曾靠傍晚六点抢电过得舒舒服服的交易员，发现自己的利润空间被压缩了。

paragraphs.en: Yet the boom has an awkward dependency. A battery earns money only if the gap between cheap and expensive hours is wide enough. As more capacity is installed, that gap narrows — the very success of storage undermines the returns that justified it. Engineers call this cannibalisation; investors call it the reason they have suddenly become cautious.
paragraphs.zh: 然而这轮热潮有一个尴尬的依赖。只有当廉价时段与高价时段之间的差距足够大时，电池才能赚钱。随着装机增加，这个差距不断收窄——储能的成功本身，正在侵蚀当初支撑它的回报。工程师称之为“自食效应”，投资者则称之为他们突然变得谨慎的原因。

paragraphs.en: The second constraint is less visible. Grid operators have discovered that a fleet of batteries behaves nothing like a power station. It responds in milliseconds, which is wonderful for frequency regulation, but it also means that software, not concrete, now determines whether the lights stay on. Regulators trained to inspect turbines are being asked to audit code.
paragraphs.zh: 第二个约束不那么显眼。电网运营商发现，一群电池的行为完全不像一座电站。它以毫秒级响应，这对调频妙不可言，但也意味着如今决定灯是否亮着的是软件，而不是混凝土。那些受训去检查涡轮机的监管者，如今被要求审计代码。

paragraphs.en: None of this makes the transition less inevitable. It makes it messier. The cheapest electricity system humanity has ever built is also the most computationally complex, and the institutions that govern it were designed for a world in which power flowed in one direction only.
paragraphs.zh: 这一切并没有让转型变得不那么必然，只是让它更凌乱。人类建造过的最便宜的电力系统，同时也是计算上最复杂的系统；而治理它的那些制度，是为一个电力只单向流动的世界设计的。

vocab.meaning_zh: 算术；（引申）盘算、经济账。change that arithmetic 意为“改变这套算法/算账方式”
vocab.example_en: Cheap storage changes the arithmetic of every power project.
vocab.example_zh: 廉价储能改变了每个电力项目的经济账。

vocab.meaning_zh: 时间套利：利用不同时间点的价差低买高卖
vocab.example_en: Storage is pure temporal arbitrage: buy at noon, sell at dusk.
vocab.example_zh: 储能就是纯粹的时间套利：正午买入，黄昏卖出。

vocab.meaning_zh: （金融）价差、利差。外刊经济版高频词，比 difference 更专业
vocab.example_en: The spread between peak and off-peak prices has narrowed.
vocab.example_zh: 峰谷价差已经收窄。

vocab.meaning_zh: 不起眼的、不光鲜的。常用来形容“枯燥但重要”的事
vocab.example_en: It is unglamorous work, but it keeps the system running.
vocab.example_zh: 这活儿不起眼，却维持着整个系统运转。

vocab.meaning_zh: 使变平；此处指削平（价格尖峰）。flatten the curve 亦为疫情期高频表达
vocab.example_en: Storage has flattened the evening price spike.
vocab.example_zh: 储能削平了傍晚的价格尖峰。

vocab.meaning_zh: 利润空间、利润率。compress margins 挤压利润
vocab.example_en: Competition compressed margins across the industry.
vocab.example_zh: 竞争挤压了整个行业的利润空间。

vocab.meaning_zh: 自食效应：新产品/新增产能侵蚀自身原有业务或利润
vocab.example_en: Solar cannibalisation is now a planning headache in Spain.
vocab.example_zh: 光伏的自食效应如今成了西班牙的规划难题。

vocab.meaning_zh: 调频：维持电网频率稳定在 50Hz 的辅助服务，储能的核心收入来源之一
vocab.example_en: Batteries earn most of their early revenue from frequency regulation.
vocab.example_zh: 电池早期收入大多来自调频服务。

vocab.meaning_zh: 不可避免的。注意搭配：it is inevitable that…
vocab.example_en: Some disruption is inevitable.
vocab.example_zh: 一定程度的混乱不可避免。

sentences.en: A battery is not a generator; it is a temporal arbitrage machine.
sentences.structure: 主干：A battery is not a generator（主系表）／分号并列：it is a machine（主系表）
sentences.analysis_zh: 典型的“否定—重述”结构：先用 not 排除读者的默认认知（电池=发电设备），再用分号给出真正的定义。分号在这里比 but 更有力，因为它把两句摆成对等的定义句，读起来像格言。写作时想给某个概念“重新定义”，可以套这个句式：X is not A; it is B.

sentences.en: As more capacity is installed, that gap narrows — the very success of storage undermines the returns that justified it.
sentences.structure: As 引导时间/伴随状语从句 + 主句 + 破折号补充 + that 引导定语从句修饰 returns
sentences.analysis_zh: 难点在 the very success：very 放在名词前表示“正是、恰恰”，强调“成功本身”就是问题根源，是全句的逻辑枢纽。后面的 that justified it 是定语从句，it 指 storage。破折号后的部分是作者下的判断，不是事实陈述，所以读外刊时要区分“事实—评论”这两层。

sentences.en: The cheapest electricity system humanity has ever built is also the most computationally complex, and the institutions that govern it were designed for a world in which power flowed in one direction only.
sentences.structure: 并列复合句：① 主语 The cheapest electricity system + 省略 that 的定语从句(humanity has ever built) + 系表 ② and 并列 + 主语 the institutions + 定语从句(that govern it) + 被动谓语 + in which 定语从句
sentences.analysis_zh: 全句三处后置修饰叠加，是外刊长句的典型写法。拆法是先抓住两个主干：system is complex / institutions were designed for a world。humanity has ever built 前省略了 that，因为先行词被最高级 the cheapest 修饰时可省。in which power flowed 是“介词+关系代词”，比 where 更书面。

background.title: 为什么是磷酸铁锂
background.text_zh: 磷酸铁锂（LFP）电池不含镍和钴，成本低、循环寿命长、热失控风险小，缺点是能量密度低于三元锂。它不适合追求续航的乘用车，却非常适合“不动的”电网储能——体积和重量不敏感，价格和寿命才是关键。这正是它近年装机暴增的技术原因。

background.title: 加州的“鸭子曲线”
background.text_zh: 加州光伏装机极大，白天净负荷被压到很低，傍晚光伏退场、居民用电上升，净负荷曲线急剧抬升，形状像一只鸭子，故称 duck curve。它带来两个问题：白天弃光、傍晚尖峰。储能正好填在这条“鸭脖子”上，所以加州成了全球最大的储能试验场。

title_en: The city that decided to stop growing
excerpt_en: Leuven voted to cap its own expansion. Five years on, its mayor has become an unlikely reference point for European politicians who suspect that growth no longer pays for itself.
body_en: For thirty years, the planning department of Leuven treated growth as a moral obligation. Every new office block was a promise of jobs; every ring road, a declaration that the city intended to remain relevant. Then, in 2019, the council did something that would have been unthinkable a decade earlier: it voted to stop.

The decision was not an act of defeat. Officials had calculated that the cost of servicing new peripheral districts — pipes, buses, school places, the quiet arithmetic of maintenance — exceeded the tax revenue those districts generated within a generation. Growth, in other words, had stopped paying for itself.

What replaced it was an unfamiliar discipline. The city now begins every project by asking what it can reuse: a warehouse becomes a swimming pool, a convent becomes student housing, a car park becomes a square. Architects complain that the briefs are impossibly constrained. They also admit that the results are more interesting than the towers they were previously asked to design.

Not everyone is persuaded. Developers argue that a city which refuses to expand is simply exporting its housing crisis to the next town, and that the young families priced out of Leuven did not vote for walkable streets — they wanted a spare bedroom. The council's answer is blunt: the alternative was a city that everyone could reach and no one could afford.

Five years on, the most striking change is not physical but political. Leuven has become a reference point for a generation of European mayors who suspect that the growth coalition their predecessors built has quietly run out of arguments. Whether it has run out of voters is a different question, and one that the next election will answer.

enrich.title_zh: 那座决定停止扩张的城市
enrich.summary_zh: 比利时鲁汶 2019 年投票决定不再向外扩张，理由是新增城区的维护成本已超过其税收贡献。五年后，它转向“只做存量改造”的城市更新模式，也成为欧洲市长们的新参照系——尽管“停止增长”是否真有选票支持，仍是未解的问题。

paragraphs.en: For thirty years, the planning department of Leuven treated growth as a moral obligation. Every new office block was a promise of jobs; every ring road, a declaration that the city intended to remain relevant. Then, in 2019, the council did something that would have been unthinkable a decade earlier: it voted to stop.
paragraphs.zh: 三十年来，鲁汶的规划部门把增长当作一种道德义务。每一栋新写字楼都是一份就业承诺；每一条环路，都是一份“本市仍要与时俱进”的宣言。然后，在 2019 年，市议会做了一件十年前不可想象的事：投票决定停下来。

paragraphs.en: The decision was not an act of defeat. Officials had calculated that the cost of servicing new peripheral districts — pipes, buses, school places, the quiet arithmetic of maintenance — exceeded the tax revenue those districts generated within a generation. Growth, in other words, had stopped paying for itself.
paragraphs.zh: 这个决定并非认输。官员们算过账：为新边缘城区提供公共服务的成本——管道、公交、学位，以及那笔沉默的维护账——在一代人的时间里超过了这些城区带来的税收。换句话说，增长已经不再为自己买单。

paragraphs.en: What replaced it was an unfamiliar discipline. The city now begins every project by asking what it can reuse: a warehouse becomes a swimming pool, a convent becomes student housing, a car park becomes a square. Architects complain that the briefs are impossibly constrained. They also admit that the results are more interesting than the towers they were previously asked to design.
paragraphs.zh: 取而代之的是一种陌生的自律。如今这座城市每个项目都先问一句：有什么可以再利用？仓库变成泳池，修道院变成学生公寓，停车场变成广场。建筑师抱怨任务书限制得几乎无法施展。他们也承认，成品比过去被要求设计的那些高楼更有意思。

paragraphs.en: Not everyone is persuaded. Developers argue that a city which refuses to expand is simply exporting its housing crisis to the next town, and that the young families priced out of Leuven did not vote for walkable streets — they wanted a spare bedroom. The council's answer is blunt: the alternative was a city that everyone could reach and no one could afford.
paragraphs.zh: 并非所有人都被说服。开发商辩称，一座拒绝扩张的城市只是把自己的住房危机出口给了邻镇；而那些被鲁汶房价挤走的年轻家庭，投票时想要的并不是适合步行的街道，而是一间多余的卧室。市议会的回答很直白：另一条路，是造出一座人人都能到达、却没人住得起的城市。

paragraphs.en: Five years on, the most striking change is not physical but political. Leuven has become a reference point for a generation of European mayors who suspect that the growth coalition their predecessors built has quietly run out of arguments. Whether it has run out of voters is a different question, and one that the next election will answer.
paragraphs.zh: 五年过去，最引人注目的变化不在城市面貌，而在政治。鲁汶成了一代欧洲市长的参照点——他们怀疑，前任们搭建起来的“增长联盟”已经悄悄耗尽了论据。至于它是否也耗尽了选民，那是另一个问题，要由下一次选举来回答。

vocab.meaning_zh: 道德义务。把政策说成“义务”，是在暗示它已不容质疑——外刊常用这种措辞点出某种默认共识
vocab.example_en: Growth was treated as a moral obligation rather than a choice.
vocab.example_zh: 增长被当成道德义务，而不是一种选择。

vocab.meaning_zh: 边缘的、外围的。peripheral districts 指城市边缘的新区；名词 periphery
vocab.example_en: Services in peripheral districts cost more per resident.
vocab.example_zh: 边缘城区的人均公共服务成本更高。

vocab.meaning_zh: 算术；（引申）一笔账、成本核算。the quiet arithmetic of maintenance 是极漂亮的暗喻
vocab.example_en: The arithmetic of maintenance is easy to ignore and hard to escape.
vocab.example_zh: 维护这笔账容易被忽视，却难以逃避。

vocab.meaning_zh: 修道院、修女院。欧洲城市更新中常见的历史建筑改造对象
vocab.example_en: The convent now houses two hundred students.
vocab.example_zh: 那座修道院如今住着两百名学生。

vocab.meaning_zh: （设计/建筑）任务书、设计要求。形容词用法 in brief 意为“简言之”
vocab.example_en: The brief allowed almost no new construction.
vocab.example_zh: 任务书几乎不允许任何新建。

vocab.meaning_zh: 因价格过高而把……挤出（某地/某市场）
vocab.example_en: Young families have been priced out of the centre.
vocab.example_zh: 年轻家庭已被市中心的高房价挤走。

vocab.meaning_zh: 适宜步行的。城市规划术语，与 car-dependent 相对
vocab.example_en: Walkable neighbourhoods command a premium.
vocab.example_zh: 适宜步行的社区有溢价。

vocab.meaning_zh: 直截了当的、不加修饰的（指言辞）；也可指钝的
vocab.example_en: Her answer was blunt: there is no money.
vocab.example_zh: 她的回答很直白：没钱。

vocab.meaning_zh: 联盟、联合体。growth coalition 指支持增长的政治—商业同盟
vocab.example_en: The growth coalition held for three decades.
vocab.example_zh: 这个增长联盟维持了三十年。

vocab.meaning_zh: 用尽、耗尽。run out of arguments 论据用尽；run out of voters 失去选民支持
vocab.example_en: The government has run out of ideas.
vocab.example_zh: 政府已经想不出办法了。

sentences.en: Every new office block was a promise of jobs; every ring road, a declaration that the city intended to remain relevant.
sentences.structure: 并列句 + 第二分句省略谓语（every ring road [was] a declaration…）
sentences.analysis_zh: 分号后省略了 was，属于“省略式并列”，让节奏更紧、更像排比。that the city intended to remain relevant 是 declaration 的同位语从句。remain relevant 是英文里很常见的软性表述，意思是“不被时代抛下”，比 survive 更体面也更含糊。

sentences.en: The city now begins every project by asking what it can reuse.
sentences.structure: 主谓宾 + by doing 方式状语 + what 引导的宾语从句
sentences.analysis_zh: by asking 表示“以……为起点”，比 start with 更强调方法而非时间。what it can reuse 是名词性从句作 asking 的宾语，注意这里 what 兼作 reuse 的宾语，不能换成 that。

sentences.en: The council's answer is blunt: the alternative was a city that everyone could reach and no one could afford.
sentences.structure: 主系表 + 冒号解释 + 定语从句 that everyone could reach and no one could afford（并列两个谓语）
sentences.analysis_zh: 冒号在这里起“摊牌”作用，直接把抽象立场翻译成一个具体画面。定语从句里 reach 与 afford 形成对照：可到达 vs 可负担，正好是城市研究的两个核心指标（accessibility 与 affordability）。这种“用从句收尾、两个动词对撞”的写法，是卫报评论版最爱的收束方式。

background.title: 鲁汶是个什么样的城市
background.text_zh: 鲁汶（Leuven）位于比利时弗拉芒大区，人口约十万，是欧洲著名的大学城，鲁汶大学（KU Leuven）是全球最古老的天主教大学之一，也是比利时最大的雇主与研究机构。这类“大学城”财政高度依赖年轻人口，却常被房价上涨反噬——学生与教职员把住房需求推高，本地年轻家庭被迫外迁。

background.title: “增长不再为自己买单”背后的财政逻辑
background.text_zh: 城市蔓延（urban sprawl）的财政陷阱在规划学界被称为“基础设施的隐性负债”：低密度新区的道路、管网、公交、学校按峰值需求建设，但税收按人均产生，人均服务成本随密度下降而上升。美国大量郊区市镇因此陷入维护性赤字。鲁汶的算账，本质上是把这张长期负债表摊到了台面上。

title_en: Why sleep has become the last luxury good
excerpt_en: The mattress industry no longer sells comfort. It sells permission — and that shift says more about work than it does about rest.
body_en: The mattress industry has always sold comfort. What it sells now, increasingly, is permission. Advertisements for eight-hundred-dollar pillows do not promise better rest so much as they promise exemption — from the notifications, the emails, the low-grade guilt of being unreachable for seven hours.

That pitch lands because sleep has become a status symbol in a way it was not twenty years ago. When workers competed on hours, staying up late was a sign of seriousness. Now that productivity is measured in output rather than presence, the person who sleeps well is presumed to think clearly, and the person who does not is presumed to be managed by their inbox.

The economics are uncomfortable. Sleep debt is distributed along the same lines as every other kind of debt: shift workers, parents of young children and anyone holding two jobs accumulate it fastest, and they are the least able to buy their way out.

Clinicians worry that the wellness industry has reframed a public-health problem as a private purchasing decision. A wearable that scores your night does not shorten your commute, dim your streetlights or give you a bedroom that is not also a study.

Still, something has shifted in the culture. Twenty years ago, admitting that you needed nine hours was a confession of weakness. Today it is closer to a flex. That may be the cheapest public-health intervention available: not a device, not a subscription, just a change in what we are permitted to say out loud.

enrich.title_zh: 为什么睡眠成了最后一种奢侈品
enrich.summary_zh: 床垫广告卖的已经不是舒适，而是“被允许失联七小时”的特权。睡眠从“懒散”变成“自律”的象征，但它同时被包装成可以花钱购买的私人选择——而真正缺觉的轮班工人、带娃父母根本买不起。作者认为，最有价值的干预其实是允许人们公开承认自己需要九小时睡眠。

paragraphs.en: The mattress industry has always sold comfort. What it sells now, increasingly, is permission. Advertisements for eight-hundred-dollar pillows do not promise better rest so much as they promise exemption — from the notifications, the emails, the low-grade guilt of being unreachable for seven hours.
paragraphs.zh: 床垫行业过去一直卖的是舒适。而它如今越来越多卖的，是“许可”。八百美元一只的枕头，广告承诺的与其说是更好的休息，不如说是一种豁免——豁免于通知、邮件，以及那种因为七小时联系不上而产生的隐隐愧疚。

paragraphs.en: That pitch lands because sleep has become a status symbol in a way it was not twenty years ago. When workers competed on hours, staying up late was a sign of seriousness. Now that productivity is measured in output rather than presence, the person who sleeps well is presumed to think clearly, and the person who does not is presumed to be managed by their inbox.
paragraphs.zh: 这套说辞之所以奏效，是因为睡眠已经成了身份象征，而二十年前并非如此。当劳动者以工时长短竞争时，熬夜是认真投入的标志。如今生产率以产出而非在场时间衡量，睡得好的人被默认为思路清晰，睡不好的人则被默认为被收件箱牵着走。

paragraphs.en: The economics are uncomfortable. Sleep debt is distributed along the same lines as every other kind of debt: shift workers, parents of young children and anyone holding two jobs accumulate it fastest, and they are the least able to buy their way out.
paragraphs.zh: 这笔经济账令人不适。睡眠债的分布跟其他所有债务一样：轮班工人、幼儿父母、以及任何打着两份工的人积累得最快，而他们恰恰最没有能力花钱把自己赎出去。

paragraphs.en: Clinicians worry that the wellness industry has reframed a public-health problem as a private purchasing decision. A wearable that scores your night does not shorten your commute, dim your streetlights or give you a bedroom that is not also a study.
paragraphs.zh: 临床医生担心，健康产业已经把一项公共卫生问题重新包装成了私人消费决策。一只给你的睡眠打分手环，并不会缩短你的通勤、调暗你的路灯，也不会给你一间不同时兼作书房的卧室。

paragraphs.en: Still, something has shifted in the culture. Twenty years ago, admitting that you needed nine hours was a confession of weakness. Today it is closer to a flex. That may be the cheapest public-health intervention available: not a device, not a subscription, just a change in what we are permitted to say out loud.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，文化上确实有些东西变了。二十年前，承认自己需要九小时睡眠等于承认软弱。今天，这更接近于一种炫耀。而这可能是最便宜的公共卫生干预：不用设备，不用订阅，只是改变一下我们被允许大声说出口的话。

vocab.meaning_zh: 许可。此处是修辞用法：商品卖的不是功能，而是“被允许”的心理感受
vocab.example_en: The ad sells permission to switch off.
vocab.example_zh: 这则广告卖的是“被允许关机”的感觉。

vocab.meaning_zh: 豁免、免除。exempt from 免除于……
vocab.example_en: Sleep offers a temporary exemption from demands.
vocab.example_zh: 睡眠提供了一种暂时的、免于被打扰的状态。

vocab.meaning_zh: 低强度的、隐隐的（用于形容情绪、炎症等）。low-grade guilt 隐隐的愧疚
vocab.example_en: She felt a low-grade anxiety all week.
vocab.example_zh: 她一整周都有一种隐隐的焦虑。

vocab.meaning_zh: 推销话术、卖点（名词）；推销（动词）。that pitch lands 意为“那套话术奏效了”
vocab.example_en: The pitch worked because it named a real anxiety.
vocab.example_zh: 这套说辞有效，因为它点出了真实的焦虑。

vocab.meaning_zh: 假定、推定（未必有证据）。be presumed to 被默认会……
vocab.example_en: Well-rested people are presumed to be competent.
vocab.example_zh: 睡眠充足的人被默认更有能力。

vocab.meaning_zh: 睡眠债：长期睡眠不足的累积亏欠
vocab.example_en: Sleep debt cannot be repaid in one long weekend.
vocab.example_zh: 睡眠债没法靠一个长周末补回来。

vocab.meaning_zh: 靠花钱脱身、花钱解决问题
vocab.example_en: Not every problem can be bought out of.
vocab.example_zh: 不是每个问题都能用钱解决。

vocab.meaning_zh: 重新框定（问题的性质）。社科与外刊评论高频动词
vocab.example_en: The industry reframed burnout as a personal failing.
vocab.example_zh: 这个行业把职业倦怠重新定义为个人失败。

vocab.meaning_zh: （俚）炫耀、显摆。近义 brag，但更口语、更网络化
vocab.example_en: Showing up rested is the new flex.
vocab.example_zh: 神清气爽地出现，成了新的炫耀方式。

vocab.meaning_zh: 干预（措施）。公共卫生语境里指有意识采取的行动
vocab.example_en: Cheap interventions are often the most effective.
vocab.example_zh: 低成本的干预往往最有效。

sentences.en: Advertisements for eight-hundred-dollar pillows do not promise better rest so much as they promise exemption.
sentences.structure: not… so much as… 结构：否定前者、肯定后者，重心在 so much as 之后
sentences.analysis_zh: not A so much as B 意为“与其说是 A，不如说是 B”，重点永远落在 B。这是外刊最高频的“位移强调”句式之一，比 but 更微妙：它不否认 A 的存在，只是把它降级。翻译时要体现“与其说……不如说……”。

sentences.en: Now that productivity is measured in output rather than presence, the person who sleeps well is presumed to think clearly.
sentences.structure: Now that 引导原因状语从句 + 主句（含 who 定语从句 + 被动谓语）
sentences.analysis_zh: now that 表示“既然、如今既然”，兼具时间与因果，比 because 更强调条件已经改变。rather than presence 里的 presence 指“在场/坐班”，与 output 构成管理学上的一对老概念。注意被动 is presumed to 后面接的是评价，不是事实，作者用被动正好保持了一种“这是社会默认，不是我说的”的距离感。

background.title: “睡眠是身份象征”的社会学背景
background.text_zh: 美国社会学家 Thorstein Veblen 在《有闲阶级论》里提出“炫耀性消费”：地位通过可见的闲暇与浪费来展示。当长时间工作不再代表高生产力，反而暗示缺乏自主权时，“睡饱”就成了新的地位信号——它暗示你能控制自己的时间表。这也是为什么硅谷高管热衷公开自己的睡眠数据。

background.title: 睡眠不平等（sleep inequality）
background.text_zh: 流行病学研究长期显示，睡眠时长与社会经济地位正相关：低收入者、少数族裔、轮班工作者的睡眠时间更短、碎片化更严重。原因不是“不自律”，而是通勤时间长、居住环境噪音、多份工作与照护责任。因此把睡眠问题归因于个人选择（买个好枕头），在公共卫生上被视为一种“责任转移”。

title_en: A community college bets on the trades — and finds a waiting list
excerpt_en: When Lorain County Community College added a welding program built around a single employer, administrators expected thirty applicants. They got two hundred and eleven.
body_en: When Lorain County Community College added a welding program built around a single employer, administrators expected thirty applicants. They got two hundred and eleven, along with a waiting list that the college has quietly stopped advertising.

The program's design is unusually specific. Students spend two years learning the exact specifications of one factory's production line, and the company pays their tuition in exchange for a three-year commitment. It is, in effect, a marriage arranged by a syllabus.

enrich.title_zh: 一所社区学院押注技术工种，结果排起了长队
enrich.summary_zh: 俄亥俄州洛雷恩县社区学院开设了一个围绕单一企业需求设计的焊接项目，原以为只有三十人报名，结果来了二百一十一人。企业代缴学费，学生承诺服务三年——一份由教学大纲撮合的“婚姻”。

paragraphs.en: When Lorain County Community College added a welding program built around a single employer, administrators expected thirty applicants. They got two hundred and eleven, along with a waiting list that the college has quietly stopped advertising.
paragraphs.zh: 当洛雷恩县社区学院推出一个围绕单一雇主需求打造的焊接项目时，校方预计会有三十人报名。结果来了二百一十一人，还附了一份学校已经悄悄不再对外宣传的候补名单。

paragraphs.en: The program's design is unusually specific. Students spend two years learning the exact specifications of one factory's production line, and the company pays their tuition in exchange for a three-year commitment. It is, in effect, a marriage arranged by a syllabus.
paragraphs.zh: 这个项目的设计具体得不同寻常。学生花两年时间学习某一家工厂生产线的精确规格，企业替他们付学费，交换条件是三年的服务承诺。实际上，这是一桩由教学大纲撮合的婚姻。

vocab.meaning_zh: （复数）技术工种、蓝领手艺行业，如焊接、电工、管道
vocab.example_en: Vocational schools are rebranding the trades.
vocab.example_zh: 职业学校正在重新包装技术工种的形象。

vocab.meaning_zh: 候补名单。pull someone off the waiting list 把某人从候补名单里捞出来
vocab.example_en: The course has a waiting list of forty.
vocab.example_zh: 这门课有四十人的候补名单。

vocab.meaning_zh: 规格、技术参数。常缩写为 spec
vocab.example_en: The parts must meet exact specifications.
vocab.example_zh: 零件必须符合精确的规格。

vocab.meaning_zh: 学费；（英）教学。美式英语中多指学费
vocab.example_en: The company covers tuition and books.
vocab.example_zh: 公司承担学费和书本费。

vocab.meaning_zh: 作为……的交换。比 for 更正式，强调对等交换
vocab.example_en: They offered housing in exchange for maintenance work.
vocab.example_zh: 他们提供住处，交换条件是做维护工作。

vocab.meaning_zh: 承诺；（这里的）服务期限。注意与 promise 的区别：commitment 含投入与约束
vocab.example_en: A three-year commitment deterred some applicants.
vocab.example_zh: 三年的服务承诺让一些申请者却步。

vocab.meaning_zh: 实际上、换言之（用于给出实质判断）
vocab.example_en: In effect, the state outsourced the training.
vocab.example_zh: 实际上，州政府把培训外包了出去。

vocab.meaning_zh: 教学大纲、课程纲要。复数 syllabuses / syllabi
vocab.example_en: The syllabus was written by the factory, not the faculty.
vocab.example_zh: 这份教学大纲是工厂写的，不是教师写的。

sentences.en: It is, in effect, a marriage arranged by a syllabus.
sentences.structure: 主系表 + 插入语 in effect + 过去分词短语作后置定语
sentences.analysis_zh: 插入语 in effect 放在系动词与表语之间，是英文里很地道的“判断性停顿”，相当于中文的“实际上，”。arranged by a syllabus 是过去分词短语修饰 marriage，把“包办婚姻”这个隐喻落到实处——教学大纲充当了媒人。用一个具体隐喻收尾，是专栏短文的常见手法。

background.title: 美国社区学院与“职业通道”
background.text_zh: 美国社区学院（community college）提供两年制副学士学位与职业证书，学费远低于四年制大学，是蓝领技术人才的主要培养渠道。近年制造业回流造成焊工、电工、数控操作员严重短缺，企业与社区学院合办“定制班”（employer-partnered programs）成为常见解法，但批评者指出，课程过度绑定单一企业会让学生在企业撤厂时失去可迁移技能。

title_en: Europe's chip subsidy race enters its awkward second act
excerpt_en: Brussels approved a second wave of semiconductor aid this week, but the plants it is paying for may open into a market that no longer needs them.
